claim_limits: 72 trials are 24 distinct synthetic injected development defects in two real C++ repositories; no production effectiveness is measured.
Independent source review and finite trusted native guards do not prove universal semantic correctness. Semantic-valid means no independently confirmed regression in the completed review.

The 2-repair/4-inspection control versus 4-repair/6-inspection arms differs in allowed inference resources. Only expanded-budget-v7 versus assertion-grounded-v7 isolates prompt at equal resource ceilings.

All 24 trials per arm remain in the primary denominator, including pre-model safe stops. A randomized native baseline mismatch before inference is not evidence that extra budget or a different prompt caused another arm to succeed. Model-reaching counts are descriptive only; no registered trial is rerun, reseeded or excluded.
Latency is descriptive and confounded by concurrent scheduling, native compilation and caches. Token fields include cached/reasoning subcounts and must not be naively added into a single token count.
Raw native publications, unsuccessful trials, provider errors, actual calls, and tokens remain unchanged and counted. No model grader is used.

residual_reviews.review: vprintf initializes fresh specs with align::right for each conversion. Before the modified integer-precision block, parse_header and parse_flags may set left alignment or fill, but never numeric alignment; the sole numeric assignment in vprintf occurs later when zero fill remains. Consequently this new numeric-to-right conditional cannot fire in this public parsing path. Existing precision zero-fill reset and all other behavior remain pinned. No contract change or input-specific workaround observed; no performance claim is made.

The negative-fraction minute-boundary fallback converts the original timepoint to time_t before decrementing one second, instead of subtracting a Duration-rounded second from the source representation. For finite ordinary fractional values that reach this branch it crosses the same integer-second boundary, preserving existing nonunit-ratio behavior. It also avoids source-Duration narrowing/overflow near minimum representation. All proof source roots remain unchanged; no test-specific values appear in the production patch.

Restores octal bound and uses generic digit-aware pre-multiply byte bound ch>(255-digit)/16. For every hex digit 0..15 this is exactly the condition that16*ch+digit exceeds 255; no overflow arithmetic is executed. Arbitrarily long leading zeros remain accepted. Immediate rejection can shorten the quoted error substring versus pinned behavior, but exact diagnostic wording and destination after failure are not public guarantees. No input-specific workaround observed. The new flag is set exactly in the two existing branches that consume a hexadecimal prefix. Each branch first requires at least two remaining bytes, so advancing two gives start<=end; a final start==end check is equivalent to each original start>=end check. There are no externally visible writes or parsing actions between the old and deferred rejection points. Inferred lone-octal zero continues to produce the same accepted empty digit span because the hex flag stays false. Invalid bases, whitespace/sign handling, value/overflow parsing and helper output parameters preserve their original behavior. No API change or input-specific workaround observed.

Restores octal bound and adds a generic sticky exceeds-byte flag. Before another digit, ch>15 means the next value necessarily exceeds 255; once flagged arithmetic is suppressed while all digits are consumed. On unflagged paths ch always remains 0..255, making the removed final ch>255 test redundant. Valid byte inputs including arbitrary leading zeros preserve values. Preventing wraparound matches documented arbitrary-length-one-byte contract. No input-specific workaround observed. Trunc is unchanged. Floor/Ceil compute truncation before normalizing sign and correct using the original representable negative unit directly when needed, avoiding AbsDuration(INT64_MIN seconds) saturating positive magnitude to infinity. Ordinary finite/nonzero unit values retain signed mathematical rounding; zero/infinite branches preserve existing behavior in the observed domain. Separate external native exact-integer quarter-tick proof .auto-fix/development-semantic-audit/duration-sign-normalization-v7-control/proof.json SHA3550c2cf6b2b05e0deb97770e4ec9a809902a95d6ffaf5749e521bcbf8b642d9 compiles this exact source SHA 1a6c105017796ec9969615fdb01a3961b466b8d9f0bb3d65bcca2581c6fbcf64 and passes 396 finite contracts, with only five mathematical-floor improvements versus pin at minimum negative units. Observed infinite-input/unit behavior matches pin. Control and expanded-budget candidates have identical full duration.cc bytes, so this exact-source proof applies to both. This is a generic contract improvement/pinned boundary difference, not test-specific output substitution or universal correctness proof.

Both output conversions replace adding divisor-1 before unsigned division with rounding the fractional remainder up to a divisor multiple when nonzero. For bounded nonnegative x and divisor b, floor((x+b-1)/b) equals x/b plus (x%b!=0), exactly the new expression after division. Time nanosecond carry boundaries (4,000,000,000 ticks per second, divisible by 4) and timeval carry boundaries (1,000,000,000ns divisible by 1000) remain identical. The different intermediate low remainders are discarded by the unchanged divisions; finite rep_lo<4e9 keeps either addition below UINT32_MAX, and nsec+999 remains below signed 32-bit max. Infinite/narrowing branches are unchanged. Final POSIX seconds/fraction outputs are equivalent, including negative integral values and carry edges. No test-specific workaround observed.

The FloorToUnit implementation and INT64_MIN underflow guard remain pinned. For ToUnixSeconds, a finite Duration represents hi whole seconds plus a nonnegative fractional second: truncating division by one second returns hi for nonnegative/integral durations, or hi+1 with negative remainder for negative fractional durations, then FloorToUnit restores hi. At finite MIN and MAX boundaries and both infinities, IDivDuration saturation plus existing MIN guard returns the same GetRepHi bound. Removing absl:: qualification in ToUniversal resolves the same local anonymous-namespace FloorToUnit. No value/API contract change or test-specific workaround observed. Division replaces direct field access, so this review makes no performance-equivalence claim.

The added !new_status.ok() skips assigning OK to an already-OK target. Pinned Status::ok() is exact equality to the canonical inline OK representation; when both objects are OK they have equal rep_. Both pinned copy and move assignment already do nothing when x.rep_ == old_rep, so the original does not consume the source in this both-OK case either. All error adoption, first-error preservation, payload sharing, and source move behavior are unchanged; self-update remains harmless. No test-specific workaround or observable value/ownership contract change found.

CloneAndUnref still copies every nonempty payload set. For an empty allocated Payloads container, it now leaves the clone payload pointer null, which GetPayload, ForEachPayload, ToString and equality already treat identically to an empty container. Later SetPayload allocates lazily and retains identical payload values; ErasePayload finds no key in either representation. Code/message/refcount semantics are unchanged. Allocation timing and address-dependent but explicitly unspecified payload iteration ordering may differ; no performance or allocation-count equivalence is claimed. No test-specific workaround found.

For a valid live StatusRep, the signed strong reference count starts at 1 and remains positive while any owning Status uses it. Under that representation invariant, <=1 and ==1 select exactly the same unique-owner fast path; shared refcounts >=2 still clone. Zero/dead objects, reference-count overflow/corruption, and concurrent mutation of the same Status are outside that invariant; this is not an all-bit-pattern equivalence claim. The acquire atomic ordering and shared-object cloning contract are preserved. No test-specific workaround observed.
